gold_sql.postgres: SELECT DISTINCT li.invoice_id, p.code, pf.feature_id FROM billing.invoice_line_items li JOIN billing.subscriptions s ON s.subscription_id = li.subscription_id JOIN billing.plans p ON p.plan_id = s.plan_id JOIN billing."PlanFeatures" pf ON pf.plan_id = p.plan_id WHERE li.subscription_id IS NOT NULL ORDER BY li.invoice_id, pf.feature_id;

gold_sql.duckdb: SELECT DISTINCT s.tenant_id FROM billing.subscriptions s JOIN billing.plans p ON p.plan_id = s.plan_id WHERE p.code LIKE 'pro%' AND s.deleted_at IS NULL AND s.tenant_id NOT IN (SELECT s2.tenant_id FROM billing.subscriptions s2 JOIN billing.plans p2 ON p2.plan_id = s2.plan_id WHERE p2.code LIKE 'enterprise%' AND s2.deleted_at IS NULL) ORDER BY s.tenant_id;
gold_sql.postgres: SELECT DISTINCT s.tenant_id FROM billing.subscriptions s JOIN billing.plans p ON p.plan_id = s.plan_id WHERE p.code LIKE 'pro%' AND s.deleted_at IS NULL AND s.tenant_id NOT IN (SELECT s2.tenant_id FROM billing.subscriptions s2 JOIN billing.plans p2 ON p2.plan_id = s2.plan_id WHERE p2.code LIKE 'enterprise%' AND s2.deleted_at IS NULL) ORDER BY s.tenant_id;
gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT DISTINCT s.tenant_id FROM billing_subscriptions s JOIN billing_plans p ON p.plan_id = s.plan_id WHERE p.code LIKE 'pro%' AND s.deleted_at IS NULL AND s.tenant_id NOT IN (SELECT s2.tenant_id FROM billing_subscriptions s2 JOIN billing_plans p2 ON p2.plan_id = s2.plan_id WHERE p2.code LIKE 'enterprise%' AND s2.deleted_at IS NULL) ORDER BY s.tenant_id;

notes: NOT IN with a subquery; the subquery's tenant_id is NOT NULL in the generator, so no NULL-trap in gold.
question: List tenant_id for tenants who have at least one non-deleted subscription on a plan whose code starts with 'pro', AND who have zero non-deleted subscriptions on a plan whose code starts with 'enterprise'. Sort ascending.

gold_sql.duckdb: SELECT t.tenant_id, c.n FROM billing.tenants t JOIN LATERAL (SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM billing.subscriptions s WHERE s.tenant_id = t.tenant_id AND s.ended_at IS NULL AND s.deleted_at IS NULL) c ON TRUE WHERE t.deleted_at IS NULL ORDER BY t.tenant_id;
gold_sql.postgres: SELECT t.tenant_id, c.n FROM billing.tenants t JOIN LATERAL (SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM billing.subscriptions s WHERE s.tenant_id = t.tenant_id AND s.ended_at IS NULL AND s.deleted_at IS NULL) c ON TRUE WHERE t.deleted_at IS NULL ORDER BY t.tenant_id;
gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT t.tenant_id, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM billing_subscriptions s WHERE s.tenant_id = t.tenant_id AND s.ended_at IS NULL AND s.deleted_at IS NULL) AS n FROM billing_tenants t WHERE t.deleted_at IS NULL ORDER BY t.tenant_id;

notes: DuckDB/Postgres use LATERAL; SQLite uses scalar correlated subquery (same result).
question: For every non-deleted tenant, return the tenant_id and the count of subscriptions where ended_at IS NULL AND deleted_at IS NULL. Use LATERAL (or a correlated subquery on sqlite). Every non-deleted tenant appears once, with 0 when they have no such subscription. Sort by tenant_id.

gold_sql.duckdb: SELECT CAST(100 * (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT d.tenant_id) FROM audit.disputes d JOIN billing.tenants t ON t.tenant_id = d.tenant_id WHERE d.status='open' AND t.deleted_at IS NULL) / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM billing.tenants WHERE deleted_at IS NULL) AS INTEGER) AS pct;
gold_sql.postgres: SELECT (100 * (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT d.tenant_id) FROM audit.disputes d JOIN billing.tenants t ON t.tenant_id = d.tenant_id WHERE d.status='open' AND t.deleted_at IS NULL) / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM billing.tenants WHERE deleted_at IS NULL))::INTEGER AS pct;
gold_sql.sqlite: SELECT CAST(100 * (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT d.tenant_id) FROM audit_disputes d JOIN billing_tenants t ON t.tenant_id = d.tenant_id WHERE d.status='open' AND t.deleted_at IS NULL) / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM billing_tenants WHERE deleted_at IS NULL) AS INTEGER) AS pct;

notes: Integer division keeps the result deterministic across engines.
